title: Redwood + AuroraCloud joint solution integration sync
summary: High-level technical sync on marketplace listing, reference architecture finalization, and joint solution go-to-market. Agreed next steps for security docs, benchmark runs, and marketplace asset handoff. Action items assigned and timeline to complete POC readiness.
next_steps: Redwood to share final reference architecture diagram and CloudFormation/Terraform snippets (Jamie)
AuroraCloud to provide required marketplace metadata and logos (Priya)
SEs to run benchmark job and share results by next week (Marco & Ethan)
Schedule security deep-dive to cover KMS/HSM and audit logs (Samir + Asha)

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-05-30
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees (Redwood): Jamie Liu (AE), Marco Diaz (SE), Asha Patel (CSM)
- Attendees (AuroraCloud): Priya Nair, Ethan Zhou, Marta Lopez, Samir Iqbal

[00:00] Jamie Liu: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, um we'll kick off — quick agenda, marketplace listing, reference arch final review, benchmarks, and security. sound good?
[00:18] Priya Nair: yeah that works for us, thanks Jamie. wanted to make sure we cover the listing asset requirements cause our marketing team needs lead time.
[00:30] Marco Diaz: great, i'll start with the reference arch, high level first. so the recommended pattern for auroracloud customers is private deployment via VPC peering or PrivateLink, with a small control plane in Redwood hosted if you choose marketplace listing. we have two flows: hosted API integration and private deployment packaged for auroracloud marketplace.
[01:02] Ethan Zhou: right, can you clarify the control plane requirements? our compliance folks prefer customer-managed control plane, minimal outbound.
[01:20] Marco Diaz: yep for enterprise customers we support private control plane option — control plane only orchestrates deployment ops, no customer data persists there. payloads stay in the customer's VPC, and we support bringing-your-own-KMS for key material. small caveat: autoscaling hooks need an egress to Redwood for billing/telemetry unless you opt for offline batch reporting.
[01:46] Samir Iqbal: that egress is my main concern; we need exact ports and endpoints for whitelist. do you have a list?
[01:55] Marco Diaz: we do, i'll send the CIDR ranges and ports after the call; for marketplace listing we include a firewall-whitelist doc.
[02:12] Marta Lopez: can we look at the reference arch diagram now?
[02:18] Jamie Liu: sure, i'm screen-sharing the diagram — sorry if the auto transcript labels it weird, but the key components: inbound requests, routing, private inference cluster on GPU nodes, KV cache, and optional prefix-caching layer.
[02:45] Priya Nair: for the marketplace we need an architecture PDF, a short 500-word description, logos, and a contact for support. what's the acceptable format?
[02:58] Asha Patel: PNG/SVG for logos, PDF for arch, markdown for the description. we'll provide a template in the partner portal.
[03:10] Ethan Zhou: performance — what numbers can we expect? our use case is multi-tenant chatbots with p95 latency under 300ms for short contexts.
[03:26] Marco Diaz: depends on model and quantization. for quantized, optimized routes we typically hit p95 ~150-250ms for 2k token sequence on A100 equivalent in dedicated mode, but hosted multi-tenant will be higher due to batching. we'll run a benchmark with your typical prompt mix.
[03:50] Ethan Zhou: perfect, can you include cost-per-token estimates so we can compare to BigCloud AI?
[03:58] Jamie Liu: yes we'll include unit-cost estimates and options: hosted, dedicated reservation, and private with committed capacity.
[04:08] Priya Nair: about security, Samir is asking about KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. can you summarize what you support?
[04:18] Marco Diaz: BYOK via KMS, HSM integrations on the private path, and comprehensive audit logs pushed to your SIEM. for marketplace listing we have a SOC2 package and a compliance checklist which i'll share.
[04:36] Samir Iqbal: do you have an SOC2 letter or just a self-attestation?
[04:41] Asha Patel: we maintain SOC2 Type II and provide the report under NDA; for private on-prem we offer a reduced scope with audit log exports.
[04:55] Marta Lopez: timeline — we're targeting listing go-live in 3 weeks to align with our marketplace cadence. is that realistic?
[05:04] Jamie Liu: three weeks is tight but feasible if we get assets and benchmarks this week. key dependencies: getting your marketplace metadata and legal sign-off, our security docs exchange, and the benchmark run.
[05:19] Priya Nair: we'll prioritize the asset pack.
[05:23] Ethan Zhou: on the benchmark, what environment should we use? mirrored to our production, or a canonical load?
[05:31] Marco Diaz: do both: canonical synthetic to validate p95 targets and a small run using a sanitized sample of your production prompts. we'll need sanitized prompts and rough prompt length distribution.
[05:48] Samir Iqbal: any PII handling in those prompts? we'll sanitize before sharing.
[05:53] Marco Diaz: perfect, sanitized is fine. we'll provide a script for running the tests and an example results dashboard.
[06:05] Jamie Liu: ok next section: marketplace listing flow — once you provide assets we create a draft listing in the partner portal, which you can review. after approval we publish. there is a validation step where marketplace runs an integration smoke test.
[06:25] Priya Nair: what's the smoke test surface?
[06:29] Jamie Liu: connectivity, auth flows (OIDC/SAML if used), basic inference sanity, and that the marketplace billing hooks are connected.
[06:38] Marta Lopez: for pricing tiers, can we support trial credits and subscription tiers?
[06:42] Jamie Liu: yes, marketplace supports trial credits, metered usage, and reserved capacity SKUs — we can map Redwood pricing models to your marketplace catalog.
[06:51] Ethan Zhou: any limitations around private deployment packaging for auroracloud marketplace?
[06:57] Marco Diaz: for private deployments we provide a deployable package (Terraform module + Helm charts) that provisions the inference cluster within the customer's account and wires up Redwood's control plane or the optional self-hosted controller. the package must be validated by marketplace security; we can help with that validation.
[07:19] Priya Nair: ok good. one item — billing connector. How do we surface usage to auroracloud marketplace for billing?
[07:28] Asha Patel: we expose a billing webhook and a usage file export; marketplace integrates either via webhook or S3 file delivery. we'll share the schema.
[07:40] Samir Iqbal: do you encrypt the billing files at rest?
[07:44] Asha Patel: yes, encrypted at rest and in transit using customer-managed keys if requested.
[07:51] Marco Diaz: quick note on failovers: in dedicated mode we provide automatic fallback to a lighter quantized model if capacity issues arise, that is part of our graceful degradation strategy.
[08:03] Ethan Zhou: would that be acceptable for our compliance team? fallback needs to be auditable.
[08:10] Samir Iqbal: we need logs that indicate when fallback occurred and which model served the request.
[08:15] Marco Diaz: we emit model-routing events to audit logs; we'll include schema details.
[08:25] Jamie Liu: jumping ahead to timeline recap — if Marco can run benchmarks by next Friday and we get assets by Wednesday, we can hit the three-week goal.
[08:35] Marta Lopez: sounds good. I'll coordinate with Priya to get assets Wednesday.
[08:40] Priya Nair: yes.
[08:42] Jamie Liu: any blockers on the security side?
[08:45] Samir Iqbal: i just need the SOC2 sample report under NDA and the KMS integration guide; then i'll confirm whitelist rules.
[08:53] Asha Patel: we'll send the SOC2 NDA link and the KMS/HSM integration doc after this call.
[09:00] Marco Diaz: quick technical question from me: for the marketplace package, do you accept Terraform modules only or also CloudFormation?
[09:08] Priya Nair: we accept both but prefer Terraform for lifecycle management.
[09:13] Marco Diaz: great we'll include TF snippets.
[09:17] Jamie Liu: any competitive concerns we should be aware of? Priya mentioned BigCloud AI earlier — are there feature gaps to call out?
[09:26] Priya Nair: BigCloud AI has an embedded A/B testing feature in their listing that our product team likes. are rollout policies supported?
[09:34] Marco Diaz: yes, Redwood supports canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallback policies; we can demonstrate in a short follow-up demo if useful.
[09:45] Ethan Zhou: that demo would be helpful for our product team.
[09:48] Jamie Liu: noted. we'll schedule a demo next week focused on rollout policies and cost controls.
[09:55] Marta Lopez: action items recap?
[09:58] Jamie Liu: jotted earlier — i'll email the arch diagram and deploy snippets; marco will run benchmarks; aasha will send SOC2 NDA and KMS docs; priya will share assets; marta will draft listing copy.
[10:15] Priya Nair: any final questions?
[10:18] Samir Iqbal: none from me, thanks.
[10:21] Jamie Liu: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and timeline.
[10:25] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains some imperfect auto-caption labels and occasional filler words. references made to partner portal and partner asset templates. Links to docs to be shared: partner-portal/templates, SOC2-NDA-link, reference-arch-diagram (links will be provided in follow-up email).
